ov: A gastropod with a coiled shell big enough to pull itself into. Land snails are the familiar ones, but most snail species live in the sea, and many more in fresh water.

why.h: Some land snails hibernate through winter, sealing the shell opening with a dried layer of mucus to stay moist. They may also go dormant in summer droughts.
why.p: Snails are occasionally kept as household pets, though land snails are better known as garden and farm pests.
why.ac: Land snails are most active at night and after rain, when the damp air keeps them from drying out.
why.et: Eaten in many cultures and farmed for food in some places.

len: 0.6 mm (shell) to 39 cm (giant African land snail)
rg: Worldwide: on land from ditches to deserts, in fresh water, and in the sea down to the abyssal depths.
df: Most land snails eat plants, living or dead. Some land snails and many sea snails are omnivores or predators.
fx: The ancient dye Tyrian purple, worn by royalty, was made from the secretions of certain sea snails.
